subject: Holi
prompt: This major Hindu spring festival of colours celebrates the love between which pair of deities?
why: Holi is a major Hindu festival of colours, love and spring. It celebrates the love between the deities Radha and Krishna, and signifies the triumph of good over evil.

subject: World population
prompt: The United Nations estimated the total number of humans alive passed eight billion on which date?
why: In world demographics, the world population is the total number of humans currently alive. It was estimated by the United Nations to have exceeded 8 billion on November 15, 2022.

subject: Saturn
prompt: The second largest planet in the Solar System is a gas giant with an average radius roughly how many times that of Earth?
why: Saturn is the sixth planet from the Sun and the second largest in the Solar System after Jupiter. It is a gas giant with an average radius about 9 times that of Earth.

subject: UEFA Conference League
prompt: UEFA's third-tier annual club football competition has been organised since which year?
why: The UEFA Conference League is an annual association football competition organised since 2021 by the Union of European Football Associations.

subject: Latin
prompt: Originally spoken by the Latins in Latium, now Lazio, this classical language belongs to which branch of Indo-European?
why: Latin is a classical language belonging to the Italic branch of the Indo-European languages. It was originally spoken by the Latins in Latium, now known as Lazio.

subject: Eurovision Song Contest 2024
prompt: The 68th edition of this song competition, with semi-finals on 7 and 9 May and a final on 11 May, was staged at the Malmö Arena — in which country?
why: The Eurovision Song Contest 2024 was the 68th edition, consisting of two semi-finals on 7 and 9 May and a final on 11 May 2024, held at the Malmö Arena in Malmö, Sweden.

subject: Harvard University
prompt: This private Ivy League research university in Cambridge, Massachusetts was founded in which year?
why: Harvard University is a private Ivy League research university in Cambridge, Massachusetts, founded in 1636 and named Harvard College in 1639 in honour of its first benefactor.

subject: Gregorian calendar
prompt: The civil calendar used in most of the world today went into effect following a papal bull, in which year?
why: The Gregorian calendar is used in most parts of the world. It went into effect in October 1582 following the papal bull Inter gravissimas.

subject: Eid al-Adha
prompt: The second of Islam's two main festivals, the Feast of the Sacrifice, falls on the 10th day of which month?
why: Eid al-Adha, the Feast of the Sacrifice, is the second of the two main festivals in Islam alongside Eid al-Fitr. It falls on the 10th of Dhu al-Hijjah.

subject: Discord
prompt: This American social platform carries text, media and video, plus voice calls delivered over the internet using which technology?
why: Discord is an American instant messaging and VoIP social platform allowing communication through voice calls, video calls, text messaging and media, privately or in communities.

subject: Brownie (folklore)
prompt: Also called a broonie or brùnaidh, this household spirit comes out at night while the owners sleep. Whose folklore is it from?
why: A brownie or broonie, also known as a brùnaidh or gruagach in Scottish Gaelic, is a household spirit or hobgoblin from Scottish folklore said to come out at night while the owners sleep.

subject: Newton's laws of motion
prompt: Providing the basis for Newtonian mechanics, these physical laws relate an object's motion to the forces acting on it. How many are there?
why: Newton's laws of motion are three physical laws that describe the relationship between the motion of an object and the forces acting on it, providing the basis for Newtonian mechanics.

subject: Budapest
prompt: Hungary's capital and primate city has a greater metro area of about 3.3 million. Roughly how many live in the city itself?
why: Budapest is the capital and most populous city of Hungary. It is Hungary's primate city with 1.7 million inhabitants, and its greater metro area has a population of about 3.3 million.

subject: Schrödinger's cat
prompt: In this thought experiment a hypothetical cat in a closed box may be considered simultaneously alive and dead. Which quantum concept is it illustrating?
why: In quantum mechanics, Schrödinger's cat is a thought experiment concerning quantum superposition, in which a hypothetical cat in a closed box may be considered simultaneously alive and dead.

subject: Chechnya
prompt: Officially the Chechen Republic, this republic of Russia sits in the North Caucasus between the Caspian Sea and which other sea?
why: Chechnya, officially the Chechen Republic, is a republic of Russia situated in the North Caucasus of Eastern Europe, between the Caspian Sea and the Black Sea.

subject: Ram Mandir
prompt: Built at a site many Hindus believe to be Ram Janmabhoomi, this temple complex in Ayodhya stands in which Indian state?
why: The Ram Mandir is a Hindu temple complex in Ayodhya, Uttar Pradesh, India. Many Hindus believe it is located at the site of Ram Janmabhoomi, the birthplace of Rama.

subject: YouTube Music
prompt: This music streaming service was developed by a video platform that is itself a subsidiary of which company?
why: YouTube Music is a music streaming service developed by the American video platform YouTube, a subsidiary of Google.
